title: 3 Days of Vibe coding with Claude + Lovable + Gemini Music
author: Comet7777
selftext:
Okay... I work with AI tools in the tech start up world, but I finally decided to branch out and see what could be possible on the game dev side. I've done some game dev side projects, but I always hit a few walls around art asset generation. 

This was the tooling breakdown:

* Coding - Claude Opus models. I had a good sense of the software architecture I needed for this game. It's really not that complex from a systems perspective. But having all of that laid out ahead of time made it easy for Claude to orchestrate between tools and assets as they came in. Also, I think what really helps was having a design document where Claude understood what the final version of this could be, so it knew when to plan for future assets or how to make certain components scalable across a single context. 
* Artwork - Surprisingly, Lovable. I am a bit of a Lovable power user since I've used it for quick high-quality prototypes in my profession. I decided to ask it to render a few pixel concepts. It killed it, I was shocked. I was fully expecting to have to spend money on some art AI tool or to level up my pixel art game. I invested in tools and books for pixel art creation and occasionally opened up things like Aseprit to touch up some stuff, but this was mostly Lovable generating the art. 
* Music - Gemini music - fairly straightforward. I come from a music background (hell my Reddit profile pic is James Hetfield's signature guitar), so I got as detailed as possible in my prompting. Also leaning on Mega Man X OST patterns made this easy for me. 
* Sound effects - ElevenLabs - got a cheap monthly subscription here to handle the sound effect creation. A game with system-generated effects sounds super cheap, so I thought this was worth it. 

  
Also, to be fair, when I say it took 3 days that's true but also not really true? The game design was done long before I started vibe coding. I had worked on this game a decade back before career and family priorities forced me to stop. So I had character concept art, maps, game design stuff all circulating in old computers ready to be resurrected from the dead. I hope this helps others who are doing AI game dev!

comments.author: Infinite-Aioli-6274
comments.body: Love the mega man mechanics! Also, insanely impressive that you were able to vibe code this in three days. My top down shooter is taking me forevvvvver.

replies.author: Comet7777
replies.body:
Thanks for that!

What’s been your biggest roadblock on your shooter?

replies.author: Infinite-Aioli-6274
replies.body:
The biggest roadblock has been figuring out difficulty and progression. In my game you can steal weapons from enemy ships. If you leave the level with the weapon, the weapon will level up. It's been challenging making sure the weapons don't level up too quickly. Also, during the missions there is chatter between the player and the bosses on the radio, so insuring that dialog makes sense with the overall story while still feeling natural (like something someone would actually say given the situation) has been tough.

What about you? Also meant to compliment your art style, it's very SNES, I love it.

replies.author: Comet7777
replies.body:
I think I’m going to run into the same issue. Difficulty can happen in many ways:

1. Enemy design gets smarter or more challenge   
2. Enemies become sponges   
3. Environmental hazards 

I love the idea of leveling up aspects of your ship. Progression is the dopamine we all love right? But then the game becomes way too easy. So I wonder if part of it is allowing a player to become godly if they want, but then added some difficulty spikes that are optional pieces of content for those that want more. 

Kinda like Elden Ring’s DLC difficulty. It was optional and insanely spiked

replies.author: Infinite-Aioli-6274
replies.body: Yeah, that is what i've been wrestling with. Currently, I'm not allowing the player to become godly, but I think I should. Replaying a level right now only grants any experience you might have missed on the first run instead of resetting. But yes, optional levels that are difficult sound like the right way to go. Thank you!!!

replies.author: Comet7777
replies.body: One thing I’m going to play around with is multiple routes in a stage with incentives to go back. That way the player isn’t just grinding experience but maybe there are unique upgrades or skins or secret bosses or who knows what else. Replayability is a bit focus for me and the exp grinding is a part of that for sure

replies.author: Infinite-Aioli-6274
replies.body: Exactly! That would be sick. I like the skins and secret bosses idea. It's those little details that keep players invested.

replies.author: Comet7777
replies.body: Yeah, and StarFox is a good model for some of that.
